A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DSpodFL work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix O report original FMNIST/SVM and CIFAR10/VGG11 experiments, including accuracy, simulated delay, and parameter-sensitivity results.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix O retain these original experiments and add resource-distribution, scalability, and learning-rate results.

M1.justification: The update rule, objective, matrix formulation, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Section 3.1 makes link symmetry and mixing-weight construction more explicit, without establishing a different procedure.

E1.justification: FMNIST and CIFAR10 image classification remain the datasets and tasks. Figures 4b and 9 add bimodal and unimodal truncated-Gaussian client/link capability populations, extending the resource-environment scenarios beyond the retained Beta and uniform cases.

E2.justification: DGD, DFedAvg, Randomized Gossip, and Sporadic SGDs remain the four empirical comparators in corresponding experiments and the added plots. Additional theoretical comparisons in Appendix P.4 do not introduce experimentally evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Added experiments use 50-client label/connectivity sweeps, vary computation and communication probabilities separately, and test learning rates {0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1}. Figure 11 evaluates accuracy at delays 500 for FMNIST and 5000 for CIFAR10. Existing experiments retain their stated settings and metrics.

E4.justification: Figure 4 and new Appendices O.7–O.9 substantially extend robustness analysis: Gaussian resource distributions, scalability combined with label/connectivity variation, separate computation-versus-communication controls, and learning-rate sensitivity. These test several distinct explanations for the reported advantage beyond v2's retained analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments are repeated and report means with one-standard-deviation uncertainty. Neither specifies exact run counts or seeds. Added plots continue the existing uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figures 4 and 9–11 add substantial results across the new sensitivity experiments. Figure 11 reports DSpodFL settings exceeding the best tested baseline accuracy, while Figure 10 shows single-sporadic baselines approaching DSpodFL as one resource type becomes more homogeneous. Existing matched plots and Tables 2–5 retain their results.

T1.justification: Assumption 4.3 replaces blanket mutual uncorrelatedness with separately specified noise and indicator conditions. Appendix E.3 corrects some equality/inequality relations; new C.1 derives an implication between heterogeneity assumptions, and P.4 develops explicit bound comparisons. Existing theorem bounds and convergence rates remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: jointly sporadic computation and communication, a unifying decentralized framework, convex/non-convex convergence guarantees, and improved accuracy-versus-delay performance. Added evidence supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix P adds explanations involving overlapping client data and baseline-specific normalized delays. Appendix O.8 interprets which sporadic component matters when communication or computation resources become more homogeneous. The stated limitation concerning larger datasets and tasks beyond image classification is unchanged.

D1.justification: A new reproducibility statement says complete training/testing code is available in supplementary material; v2 has no equivalent access statement. Section 3.1 also spells out mixing-weight details. The supplied PDFs establish the disclosure, but do not allow verification of the supplementary code.

R1.justification: v3 adds Brinton et al. (2024), Saha et al. (2024), and Cortes and Vapnik (1995). Appendix P.4 expands convergence comparisons with already-cited research, while the central novelty positioning and Table 1 comparison remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain intact. v3 adds explanatory subsections and a reproducibility statement, clarifies proof steps, corrects cross-references, and updates citation style, affiliation information, and publication headers.

P2.justification: Four new multipart figures—4 and 9–11—substantially expand the experimental displays. Figure 4 sits beside running text, and existing figures and tables are reflowed into the conference layout. v2 Figures 4–7 are retained as v3 Figures 5–8, rather than removed.

improvement.justification: The added resource-distribution, controlled-component, and learning-rate tests strengthen confidence that the reported delay advantage is not confined to the original settings. Expanded mathematical and delay-metric explanations also improve assessability. These are useful incremental gains around an unchanged algorithm and retained principal results, rather than a substantial transformation of the paper.
